_meta.note: Explainable rule layer for crime classification and provision shortlisting. Every provision carries the plain-language reason shown to the user, so no suggestion is a black box. Codes: 'IPC:<n>' resolves against the statute knowledge base built from the uploaded dataset; 'X:<code>' resolves against extra_provisions.json.
_meta.scoring: category_score = 1.0 per strong keyword hit + 0.35 per weak hit, minus 0.9 per negative hit; provision_score = category_score * provision.weight, gated by 'requires' elements.

categories.label: Theft

elements.label: Taken without consent of the possessor
Taken from a dwelling house / building
Taken by an employee / person in service

provisions.reason: The complaint describes movable property being taken out of the complainant's possession without consent, which is the core element of theft.
The property was taken from a dwelling house, building or tent, which is an aggravated form of theft.
The complaint indicates the property was taken by a clerk or servant in the complainant's employment.
If the stolen property is later found in another person's possession, receiving stolen property may also arise.

categories.advisory: Under BNS 303(2) the value of the stolen property matters: theft below Rs. 5,000 by a first-time offender has been held to be non-cognizable, which changes how the complaint is registered. Record the approximate value.

categories.label: Snatching
strong: took from my hand and ran

elements.label: Taken directly from the person or their possession
Offenders used a vehicle to flee

provisions.reason: The property was seized suddenly and forcibly from the complainant's person, which is snatching - a distinct offence created by the BNS, 2023 with no IPC equivalent.
Snatching is a form of theft, so the general theft provision is also engaged. For an offence before 1 July 2024 only the theft provision was available.
If force caused hurt or the fear of instant hurt during the taking, the offence may rise to robbery rather than snatching.

elements.label: Force, or fear of instant hurt, used for the taking
Property taken during the same incident

provisions.reason: Property was taken using force or the fear of instant hurt, which converts theft into robbery.
Hurt was voluntarily caused in the course of committing the robbery.
A deadly weapon appears to have been used at the time of the robbery.
Where five or more persons conjointly commit robbery, the offence becomes dacoity.

elements.label: Entry into a house or building
Breaking, or entry by an unusual means
Committed after sunset and before sunrise

provisions.reason: Lurking house-trespass or house-breaking by night in order to commit an offence punishable with imprisonment.
House-breaking or lurking house-trespass in order to commit an offence.
Property was taken from inside a dwelling house after the entry.
Entry into the complainant's house without lawful authority amounts to house-trespass.

categories.label: Vehicle Theft

elements.label: Vehicle was parked / left at a place

provisions.reason: A motor vehicle is movable property; taking it without the owner's consent is theft.
Relevant at the recovery stage if the vehicle is found in another person's possession.

categories.advisory: Record the registration number, chassis number, engine number, make/model and colour. These are required for the vehicle to be entered in the national stolen-vehicle database.

categories.label: Lost Property (no offence disclosed)

elements.label: No person is alleged to have taken the property

provisions.reason: On the facts stated, the property was mislaid rather than taken by any person, so no penal offence is disclosed and a lost-property acknowledgement is the correct record.

categories.advisory: A lost-property acknowledgement is sufficient for duplicate documents, SIM re-issue and insurance. If it later emerges that a person took the property, the report should be converted into a theft case.

categories.label: Assault / Causing Hurt

elements.label: Committed by a group of persons

provisions.reason: Bodily pain or injury was voluntarily caused to the complainant.
Hurt was caused by a weapon or by means likely to cause death, which is an aggravated form.
The described injury (such as a fracture or loss of function) may amount to grievous hurt.
Grievous hurt caused by a dangerous weapon or means.
Use of criminal force or assault, where no injury is established.
Where several persons acted together with a common intention, each is liable for the act.
Where five or more persons formed an unlawful assembly and used force, rioting may be attracted.

categories.advisory: A medical examination report (MLC) is essential to determine whether the hurt is simple or grievous. The provision finally applied depends on that report.

elements.label: Threat of injury to person, reputation or property
Threat was to cause death or grievous hurt

provisions.reason: A threat of injury was made with intent to cause alarm to the complainant.
The intimidation was conveyed anonymously or by concealed identity.
Intentional insult with intent to provoke a breach of the peace.
The definitional provision for criminal intimidation, cited with the punishing section.

categories.label: Harassment / Offence against a Woman

elements.label: Complainant or victim is a woman
Physical contact or use of criminal force
Repeatedly followed or contacted despite disinterest
Victim appears to be under 18 years

provisions.reason: Criminal force was used against a woman with intent to outrage her modesty.
The described conduct - unwelcome physical advances, sexually coloured remarks or demands - falls within sexual harassment.
The complainant describes being repeatedly followed or contacted despite a clear lack of interest.
Words, gestures or acts intended to insult the modesty of a woman.
Capturing or disseminating images in circumstances that violate privacy may amount to voyeurism.
Capturing or transmitting an image of a private area without consent is separately punishable under the IT Act.
The victim appears to be a child, which makes the POCSO Act mandatorily applicable in addition to the BNS.

categories.advisory: Where the complainant is a woman, her statement should be recorded by a woman police officer. If the victim is a child, POCSO procedure and the Special Juvenile Police Unit apply, and reporting is mandatory.

categories.label: Domestic Violence / Cruelty by Husband or Relatives

elements.label: Death of a woman within seven years of marriage

provisions.reason: The complaint alleges cruelty by the husband or his relatives towards a married woman.
A demand for dowry is separately punishable under the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
Physical hurt was voluntarily caused to the complainant.
Retention of the woman's stridhan (her own jewellery and articles) may amount to criminal breach of trust.
Death of a woman in connection with a dowry demand within seven years of marriage is dealt with as dowry death.
Civil reliefs - protection, residence, maintenance and custody orders - are available in parallel and the police must inform the aggrieved woman of them.

categories.advisory: This category carries both a criminal and a civil track. The complainant should be informed of the Protection Officer and the One Stop Centre in the district.

categories.label: Cyber Fraud / Online Financial Fraud

elements.label: Committed using a phone, computer or the internet
The complainant was deceived into parting with money or credentials
OTP, password or unique identifier was misused

provisions.reason: The complainant was deceived and thereby dishonestly induced to part with money or property.
Cheating by personation using a communication device or computer resource is a distinct offence under the IT Act.
Fraudulent use of another person's password, OTP or unique identification feature is identity theft under the IT Act.
Cheating by personation, where the accused pretended to be someone else.
Where money was entrusted and then dishonestly misappropriated, criminal breach of trust may also arise.

categories.advisory: Time is critical. The complainant should immediately call the national cyber-crime helpline 1930 and file at cybercrime.gov.in so that the transaction can be put on hold. Preserve SMS, transaction IDs, the beneficiary account number and screenshots.

categories.label: Cheating / Fraud

elements.label: The complainant was induced to part with property
Indication of dishonest intention from the start

provisions.reason: The complainant was dishonestly induced to deliver property as a result of deception.
Property entrusted to the accused was dishonestly converted to their own use.
A document appears to have been forged for the purpose of cheating.
A forged document appears to have been used as genuine.
The making of a false document is punishable as forgery.
Where two or more persons agreed to commit the offence, criminal conspiracy may be added.

categories.advisory: A purely contractual breach is not a criminal offence. The distinguishing feature is dishonest intention at the time the promise was made - the officer should look for that on the facts.

elements.label: By a clerk, servant or agent
By a public servant or banker

provisions.reason: Property lawfully entrusted to the accused was dishonestly converted to their own use.
The breach of trust was committed by a clerk or servant.
The breach of trust was committed by a public servant, banker, merchant or agent.
Where there was no entrustment but property was found and dishonestly retained, misappropriation applies instead.
Wrongful loss or damage was caused to the complainant's property.
Mischief committed by fire or an explosive substance with intent to cause damage.
Mischief by fire with intent to destroy a house or a building used as a dwelling or place of worship.
The definitional provision for mischief, cited with the punishing section.

categories.label: Criminal Trespass / Encroachment

elements.label: Entry into property in the complainant's possession
Entry was into a dwelling house
Entry was for the purpose of an offence or intimidation

provisions.reason: Entry into property in the complainant's possession with intent to intimidate, insult or annoy is criminal trespass.
The trespass was into a building used as a human dwelling, which is house-trespass.
House-trespass after preparation for causing hurt, assault or wrongful restraint.

categories.advisory: Title and possession disputes over land are frequently civil in nature. A criminal provision applies only where the entry was made with the intent described in the section.

categories.label: Missing Person
strong: left the house and did not return
went out and never came back

elements.label: A person, not property, is missing
The missing person is a child under 18
Suspicion of kidnapping or foul play

provisions.reason: The report concerns a missing person and must be recorded immediately without waiting for any time period to elapse.
Where the missing person is a child, the Supreme Court's directions require an FIR on the presumption of possible kidnapping until the contrary appears.
Facts suggesting that the person was taken away against their will attract kidnapping or abduction with intent to confine.
Kidnapping or abducting a woman to compel her marriage or for illicit intercourse.

categories.advisory: Record a full physical description, recent photograph, clothing worn, mobile number and the last-seen place and time. For a missing child, an FIR must be registered forthwith and the details uploaded to the national tracking portal.

elements.label: Victim is a minor or of unsound mind

provisions.reason: A person was taken away from lawful guardianship or from India without consent.
Kidnapping accompanied by a demand for ransom is a distinct and graver offence.
Kidnapping or abducting a woman to compel her marriage or for illicit intercourse.
Kidnapping or abducting with intent secretly and wrongfully to confine the person.
The definitional provision for abduction, cited with the punishing section.

categories.label: Wrongful Restraint / Confinement
strong: did not allow me to leave

provisions.reason: The complainant was voluntarily obstructed from proceeding in a direction they had a right to proceed in.
The complainant was wrongfully confined within circumscribing limits.

categories.label: Road Accident / Rash and Negligent Driving

provisions.reason: Driving on a public way in a manner rash or negligent so as to endanger human life.
Hurt was caused by an act so rash or negligent as to endanger human life or personal safety.
Grievous hurt was caused by a rash or negligent act.
Death was caused by a rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide.
Driving at a speed or in a manner dangerous to the public is separately punishable under the Motor Vehicles Act.
The driver failed in the statutory duty to stop, secure medical attention and report the accident.

categories.advisory: Under BNS 106 the punishment is higher where the driver escapes without reporting. Record the offending vehicle number, the exact spot, and whether an ambulance or a good samaritan assisted.

categories.label: Homicide

elements.label: Committed by a group of five or more

provisions.reason: The facts allege an intentional causing of death, which is murder.
Where intention falls short of murder - for example a sudden quarrel without premeditation - the offence is culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
An act was done with such intention or knowledge that, had death been caused, it would have been murder.
Murder by a group of five or more on a ground such as caste, community or personal belief is separately dealt with under the BNS.
Where the body or evidence was concealed or destroyed, causing disappearance of evidence may also arise.
Where several persons acted in furtherance of a common intention, each is liable for the act.

categories.advisory: This is a grave offence requiring immediate officer attention, inquest proceedings and a scene-of-crime team. This draft is only a record of what the informant stated.

elements.label: Complainant put in fear of injury
Money or property delivered, or demanded
Fear of death or grievous hurt induced

provisions.reason: The complainant was intentionally put in fear of injury and thereby induced to deliver property.
Extortion by putting a person in fear of death or grievous hurt.
The threat itself is separately punishable as criminal intimidation.
Where private images are involved, the IT Act privacy provision is also engaged.

categories.label: Defamation

elements.label: An imputation was made about the complainant
It was published to third parties

provisions.reason: An imputation harming the complainant's reputation was published to others.
The definitional provision for defamation, cited with the punishing section.
Where the material published in electronic form is obscene, the IT Act provision is also engaged.

categories.advisory: Defamation is normally a non-cognizable offence pursued by private complaint before a Magistrate rather than by police FIR. The complainant should be informed of this route.

elements.label: Force or violence used by the assembly

provisions.reason: Five or more persons used force in prosecution of a common object, which is rioting.
Rioting while armed with a deadly weapon.
Every member of the unlawful assembly is liable for the offence committed in prosecution of the common object.
Being a member of an unlawful assembly.

categories.label: Suicide / Abetment of Suicide

provisions.reason: An unnatural death requires an inquest under the procedural code before any offence is determined.
Facts alleging instigation or harassment that drove the deceased to suicide attract abetment of suicide.
Cruelty by the husband or his relatives, where the deceased was a married woman.
Death of a woman within seven years of marriage connected to a dowry demand is treated as dowry death.

categories.advisory: Handle with care and sensitivity. The informant should be offered support services. Nothing in this draft determines the cause of death, which is for the inquest and post-mortem to establish.

elements.label: Occurred in or near a public place

provisions.reason: Obscene acts or words in a public place to the annoyance of others.
Intentional insult with intent to provoke a breach of the peace.
Where the complainant's movement was obstructed, wrongful restraint may also apply.
